title: Element values are not restored properly after `st.rerun`
body: ### Summary Values of components which appear after `st.experimental_rerun()` are not restored but initialized after executing `st.experimental_rerun()` ### Steps to reproduce Code snippet: [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-3533) ```python import streamlit as st radio_value = st.radio("Select1", ["Egg", "Spam", "Bacon", "Sausage"]) st.write(radio_value) if st.button("Rerun"): st.experimental_rerun() radio_value = st.radio("Select2", ["Egg", "Spam", "Bacon", "Sausage"]) st.write(radio_value) radio_value = st.radio("Select3", ["Egg", "Spam", "Bacon", "Sausage"]) st.write(radio_value) ``` 1. At first, all radio values are "Egg" 2. Change the selections; for example, "Spam", "Bacon", and "Sausage" for 3 radios respectively. Now, each radio button and its successive `st.write()` shows the selected item name. 3. Click the "Rerun" button. This triggers `st.experimental_rerun()` 4. After `st.experimental_rerun()`, **the second and third `st.write()`'s outputs are reset to "Egg"** (radio buttons selections are visually not changed though). * Rerunning without `st.experimental_rerun()` fixes this wrong state. For example, after changing the selection of some radio button which causes the script to rerun, all the component values are restored properly again. **Expected behavior:** At step 4 above, all component values are restored properly so that the second `st.write()` shows "Bacon" and the third "Sausage". **Actual behavior:** As explained above, at step 4, the second and third `st.write()` show wrong restored component values. ### Is this a regression? That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past? no ### Debug info - Streamlit version: `Streamlit, version 0.83.0` - Python version: `Python 3.8.7` - Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex?: `pyenv` + `python -m venv` - OS version: macOS Big Sur, 11.4 - Browser version: Brave 1.26.74 Chromium: 91.0.4472.124（Official Build） （arm64）

comments.body: Thanks for reporting this issue, [USER]! I was able to reproduce the behavior with `Streamlit, version 0.83.0`. The issue is no longer reproducible after the fix in the latest [`0.84.1` patch](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/releases/tag/0.84.1). Closing this issue for now.
[USER] I found this bug has been introduced again from v0.86.0.

Hi [USER],

I noticed your last reply on this issue while looking into #3854. Sorry about this getting dropped! I'll see if I can get a fix out for this in the next 2-3 weeks.

Really annoying bug. Still exists in 2024. Here's another example.

Switch the toggle, then press the st.rerun button. Toggle will now return False despite being shown as enabled.
After clicking the "do nothing" button everything becomes normal.

```python
if st.button('st.rerun'):
    st.rerun()

st.button('do nothing button')

st.write(st.session_state)

value = st.toggle('Toggle', key='toggle_value')
st.write(value)

st.write(st.session_state)
```

I did a quick investigation on this issue today. It is related to us not treating a rerun triggered by `st.rerun` as a premature_stop:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/10028f83114f71e8d826370d34abcc92aa847224/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/exec_code.py#L105

 -> This causes us to clear out all the stale widget states in the backend, which is the root cause for this issue. But just switching `premature_stop` to `False`  most likely brings in other issues and will require more investigation.

bumping this issue -- it makes st.checkbox unusable for a number of use-cases where st.rerun is required. I've not yet found a chack to make st.checkbox + button that calls st.rerun work in the meantime... but if someone else has that would be cool

The best I've got is to make a button that acts like checkbox as follows

```python
if 'toggle' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['toggle'] = False

def change_toggle():
    st.session_state.toggle = not st.session_state.toggle

st.button(label="Toggle",
          key='toggle-button',
          type='primary' if st.session_state.toggle else 'secondary',
          on_click=change_toggle)
```
Changing the `type` between primary/secondary does change the color of the button.

Or even more simply you can just replace st.checkbox with the `toggle_button` function below

```python
def toggle_button(label, key=None, help=None, on_click=None, args=None, kwargs=None, *, icon=None, disabled=False, use_container_width=False) -> bool:

    def toggle():
        st.session_state[key] = not st.session_state.get(key, False)

        if on_click is not None:
            on_click()

    return st.button(label=label,
                     key=key + '-button',
                     help=help,
                     type='primary' if st.session_state.get(key, False) else 'secondary',
                     on_click=toggle,
                     args=args,
                     kwargs=kwargs,
                     icon=icon,
                     disabled=disabled,
                     use_container_width=use_container_width)


```
